newsitem.title: FRANCE: Brunei may open Paris investment agency office.
newsitem.headline: Brunei may open Paris investment agency office.

text.p: The oil-rich state of Brunei is considering opening a Paris office for its Brunei Investment Agency to manage its portfolio investment in France, the agency managing directer said on Wednesday.

Abdul Aziz Abdul Rahman told reporters here he had met the French treasury director Jean Lemierre at the finance ministry on Wednesday for talks about opening an office to handle agency's French investments which are currently managed from London and Brussels.
The office could be "opened within a year," he said and would follow more closely the French market.
Opening a Paris office did not mean increasing the asset allocation for France but was intended to boost efficiency, he said. The London and Brussels offices would continue.
The agency invests revenues from the sultanate's oil and gas receipts in its fund for future generations.

Because of its long-term the agency invests more conservatively than mutual funds and has about half its assets in government bonds, which includes cash holdings, he said. It invests in equities as well as property, including hotels.

Brunei owns the Dorchester hotel in London and the Beverly Hills hotel in the United States. It is also training Brunei nationals in the hotel business, an official of the Brunei ministry for industry and primary resources said.
Industry sources said earlier this month Saudi billionaire Prince al-Waleed bin Talal bought the prestigious Paris hotel George V, which had caught the eye of the Sultan of Brunei.
Agency and minstry officials declined to give details of asset allocation details.
